response.answer: Seungmoon Song is a leading researcher in vision-driven locomotion and deep reinforcement learning, focusing on neuromechanical simulation and autonomous robot locomotion. He has published extensively on neuromechanical models and control systems for rehabilitation and robotics. His work includes developing predictive simulations for assistive devices.

results.title: [PDF] Seungmoon Song - Northeastern University College of Engineering
results.content: Abstract: I will present my research towards predictive simulations of human movement for assistive devices and rehabilitation treatment. In the later part, I will present recent projects on conducting a human experiment with gait assistive exoskeletons and using deep reinforcement learning to developing complex control models. In the experimental study, we found using human-in-the-loop optimization that it is possible to substantially increase self-selected walking speed with ankle exoskeletons. At last, I will discuss my plan of incorporating rigorous experimental validations and advanced computational techniques toward neuromechanical models that could change the way we design rehabilitation treatment and study human movement. His research focuses on modeling the neuromechanics of human movement and applying it to rehabilitation and robotics. During his Ph.D. at the Robotics Institute of Carnegie Mellon University, he proposed a reflex-based control model that could explain various aspects of human locomotion including diverse locomotion behaviors of healthy adults, responses to unexpected disturbances, and performance degradation in aging.
